organizations.normalization_notes: Student and employment relationships are modeled separately; Cater's attendance is not treated as employment.
The 1968 CIA memorandum prints the historical name as Eastern Air Lines; that form is preserved.
Modeled as a government assignment, not a civilian employer for the site's employer-only analytics.

affiliations.research_notes: The Congressional Record explicitly says Cater interrupted his Harvard education to serve in OSS. Harvard is an institutional student affiliation, not an employer.
Houts supplied a continuous chronology placing Eastern Air Lines in February-March 1944 immediately before April 1944 Army entry and service with OSS.
This earlier government assignment ended before a documented unemployment interval and the Eastern Air Lines job; it is not the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
The reputable biographical source supplies the sequence but does not name the brokerage or identify Lester's exact title. No organization is invented.

claims.claim_text: The indexed S. D. Cater Jr. is strongly matched to Silas Douglass Cater Jr., the Harvard student who served as an OSS Russian specialist.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index supplies Cater, S., Jr., with middle initial D; the Congressional Record gives the full name and directly documents the Harvard-to-OSS sequence.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The uncommon surname, first and middle initials, suffix and explicit OSS service make a namesake collision unlikely.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official tribute places Cater at Harvard immediately before his education was interrupted for wartime OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The match is high-confidence rather than confirmed because the tribute does not print the Box 113 identifier.

claims.claim_text: Cater's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation was student status at Harvard University.
claims.evidence_excerpt: interrupting his education to serve as a Russian specialist in the Office of Strategic Services in World War II
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Congressional Record says Cater attended Harvard and interrupted his education to serve as an OSS Russian specialist.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The initials, suffix and distinctive surname match the indexed record, and the source explicitly documents OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The wording explicitly makes Harvard education the activity interrupted by OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Harvard is presented as an institutional affiliation and student status, not as an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Marshall W. Houts is strongly matched to Marshall Wilson Houts, whose official CIA chronology records U.S. Army service with OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: April 1944 -- March 1946, in U.S. Army (served with OSS).
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NARA index and the declassified CIA memorandum share the exact first name, surname and middle initial; the memorandum expands the middle name and directly records OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact name pattern, uncommon surname and direct OSS statement support a high-confidence match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The memorandum dates Army service with OSS from April 1944 through March 1946.
claims.match_notes: The match remains high-confidence rather than confirmed because the memorandum does not print the NARA Box 351 identifier.

claims.claim_text: Houts's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation was employment as an Operations Agent with Eastern Air Lines.
claims.evidence_excerpt: February 1944 -- March 1944, Operations Agent, Eastern Air Lines.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Houts's self-supplied chronology places the Eastern Air Lines job immediately before April 1944 Army entry and OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact name pattern and explicit OSS service link the memorandum's subject to the indexed person with high confidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: The month-level chronology is continuous: Eastern Air Lines in February-March 1944, then Army service with OSS beginning April 1944.
claims.match_notes: The source directly names the employer, role and dates; no intervening affiliation is shown.

claims.claim_text: Eastern Air Lines was Houts's last documented civilian employer before the Army service during which he served with OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: February 1944 -- March 1944, Operations Agent, Eastern Air Lines.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official chronology identifies Eastern Air Lines as the last employment entry before Houts entered the Army in April 1944.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The direct OSS statement and exact name pattern support the indexed-person match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Month-level dates show the employment ended one month before Army entry; no later civilian employer appears.
claims.match_notes: This claim is kept distinct from the immediate-affiliation claim even though both refer to the same documented employment.

claims.claim_text: Houts served as an FBI Special Agent from October 1941 through December 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The self-supplied chronology records Houts's FBI special-agent service, including assignments under newspaper cover in Rio de Janeiro and as an assistant legal attaché in Havana.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact name and OSS chronology strongly identify the indexed person.
claims.temporal_assessment: The FBI assignment is definitely pre-OSS but ended before a documented unemployment interval and Eastern Air Lines employment.
claims.match_notes: The FBI is modeled as an earlier government assignment, not as Houts's immediate employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Jane Lester is strongly matched to the New York woman described as an OSS typist and later Nuremberg research analyst.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A reputable biographical account directly names Jane Lester and says she became an OSS typist; the USC Shoah Foundation independently profiles a New York-born Jane Lester of the same wartime cohort and language background at Nuremberg.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact name, direct OSS role, New York background, German fluency and immediate postwar Nuremberg work form a specific, coherent match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The book gives a continuous prewar Germany-to-Buffalo-to-OSS sequence, followed by the 1945 Nuremberg assignment corroborated by USC.
claims.match_notes: The identity is high-confidence rather than confirmed because neither external source prints the NARA Box 447 identifier.

claims.claim_text: A reputable biographical source indicates that Lester worked at an unidentified Buffalo brokerage immediately before becoming an OSS typist.
claims.evidence_excerpt: worked in a brokerage in Buffalo, then became a typist in Washington...for the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The account explicitly sequences a Buffalo brokerage job before Lester's move to Washington as an OSS typist.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact name, explicit OSS role and corroborating New York and German-language details support a high-confidence identity match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The word 'then' explicitly places the brokerage before the OSS role, but the source does not supply exact dates.
claims.match_notes: The employer remains unnamed and the role title is not reported; the public profile must keep those limits visible.

claims.claim_text: The unnamed Buffalo brokerage is Lester's last documented civilian employer before OSS service in the accessible source reviewed.
claims.evidence_excerpt: worked in a brokerage in Buffalo, then became a typist in Washington...for the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The biographical sequence identifies no intervening employer between the Buffalo brokerage and Lester's OSS typist role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The direct OSS statement and corroborating biographical details support a high-confidence match to the indexed Jane Lester.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sequence is explicit, but exact employment and OSS start dates remain unavailable.
claims.match_notes: This remains a qualified claim because a single reputable secondary account supports the employment chronology and does not name the brokerage.

research_attempts.query_text: "S D Cater Jr" OSS; "S. Douglass Cater" OSS; Harvard; Russian specialist; NARA index; CIA Reading Room; obituary; institutional and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar career sources that did not establish pre-OSS chronology were excluded from the affiliation claim.
research_attempts.research_notes: The official Congressional Record supplies the full name and explicit Harvard-to-OSS sequence. The NARA index page was visually verified.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 113 for exact dates and any separate paid employment.

research_attempts.query_text: "Millard A Copeland" OSS; "14122318"; employer 1940; occupation; NARA index; CIA Reading Room; Army enlistment; obituary; Brunswick directories and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: The Millard A. Copeland listed by the City of Brunswick as a later mayor and same-name business-directory entries lacked a matching service number, birth detail or OSS linkage; people-finder and genealogy results were also rejected.
research_attempts.research_notes: The exact private service number produced no accessible independent record. The official AAD interface was unavailable to this research session, and the same-name Brunswick candidate remains unassigned.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 143 and Army enlistment records keyed to the service number.

research_attempts.query_text: "Jacques Delmas" OSS; French Resistance; BCRA; employer; occupation; NARA index; CIA Reading Room; Ordre de la Libération; obituary and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: The Ordre de la Libération biography of Jacques Chaban-Delmas and a La Dépêche obituary for a separate Toulouse-born Resistance figure named Jacques Delmas both lacked a direct OSS, Box 178, birth-date or mission linkage to the index row.
research_attempts.research_notes: The index supplies only the name and note French. A name match alone cannot choose among multiple Resistance-era candidates, so both plausible alternatives remain visible but unassigned.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 178 and French Resistance personnel files for discriminating identifiers.

research_attempts.query_text: "Grier Durant" OSS; "L Grier DuRant"; employer 1940; occupation; NARA index; CIA Reading Room; government manual; obituary and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: A postwar U.S. Government Manual entry for L. Grier DuRant and genealogy leads for Livingston Grier DuRant did not directly establish OSS service, a pre-OSS chronology or a Box 207 linkage.
research_attempts.research_notes: The plausible expanded-name candidate remains unassigned because the accessible evidence is postwar and correlative only.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 207 for a full name and record-specific identifiers.

research_attempts.query_text: "Marshall W Houts" OSS; "Marshall Wilson Houts"; Eastern Air Lines; FBI; NARA index; CIA Reading Room; obituary; university and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Later-career summaries and an obituary that compressed the FBI-to-OSS sequence were retained only as discovery context because the declassified official chronology was more specific.
research_attempts.research_notes: NARA record 104-10104-10339 was downloaded from the official release page, all three pages were rendered, and the employment chronology on page 2 was visually inspected.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 351 for the precise OSS assignment.

research_attempts.query_text: "Shigekata Ikeda" OSS; employer; occupation; NARA index; CIA Reading Room; Japanese American; Manzanar; WRA; newspaper, directory and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Digitized War Relocation Authority rosters held by the University of California, Berkeley contain the same name but no direct OSS, Box 362 or corroborating identity link; genealogy and search-snippet leads were also rejected.
research_attempts.research_notes: The WRA records were treated only as identity leads. Unrelated sensitive personal details were neither retained nor published.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 362 for age, nationality, language or assignment identifiers.

research_attempts.query_text: "Jane Lester" OSS; "Office of Strategic Services" typist; Buffalo brokerage; employer; NARA index; CIA Reading Room; Nuremberg; obituary, oral history and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar records that only established Lester's later Nuremberg work were not used as sole evidence for her pre-OSS employment; no brokerage name was inferred from Buffalo directories.
research_attempts.research_notes: The biographical account directly supplies the brokerage-to-OSS sequence, while the USC Shoah Foundation profile independently corroborates the New York, German-language and Nuremberg identity context.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 447 and Buffalo city directories to identify the brokerage.

research_attempts.query_text: "Jackson E Nordin" OSS; employer 1940; occupation; NARA index; CIA Reading Room; military; obituary; newspaper, directory, institutional and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Modern namesakes, bare search snippets and records without the middle initial, a pre-OSS date or an OSS connection were rejected.
research_attempts.research_notes: The completed online protocol and visual index review did not identify a reliable external candidate or pre-OSS affiliation.
